title: Grid Lab: tracks, gaps, placement, auto-fit
learningObjectives: Explain grid lab: tracks, gaps, placement, auto-fit and specify the acceptance requirements for an interactive CSS lab.

understand.concept: A Grid Lab lets learners change columns, rows, gaps, track sizing, placement, and auto-fit behaviour. The preview should show the actual grid and generated CSS, including implicit tracks when they occur.
understand.whyItMatters: Separate container settings from item placement settings. Provide responsive testing, clear labels, and a reset. Explain why minmax(0,1fr) or minmax(minimum,1fr) may be needed for content sizing.
understand.analogy: A Grid Lab is a floor-plan workbench: learners change the track plan and observe where items fit.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy describes the learning workflow; the real lab must use a working preview, safe state handling, and accessible interaction.

explain.narrative: The starter uses auto-fit and minmax() to create a responsive grid. Interactive track and placement controls are the build task.

examples.explanation: The starter uses auto-fit and minmax() to create a responsive grid. Interactive track and placement controls are the build task.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered starter preview connected to editable learner controls.

practise.guidedTask: Add controls for column count, gap, min track size, and item span. Show the generated CSS and test at narrow and wide preview widths.
practise.independentTask: Implement the lab with a live isolated preview, editable controls, generated CSS, reset behaviour, and helpful error states. Test keyboard and mobile operation.
hints: Do not substitute static artwork for a real rendered preview.
Keep learner code isolated from the parent app and its secrets.
Use one source of state for controls, preview, and generated CSS.

questions.prompt: Which CSS function is commonly combined with auto-fit to set a minimum card width and flexible maximum?
questions.explanation: minmax() defines the minimum and maximum sizing functions for each repeated track.
